label: Unlinked readings from Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae
summary: I q.10 a.3 co. and ad 2: aeternitas vere et proprie in solo Deo est: The proper and participated uses are explicitly distinguished. The extant attribute premise asks whether the selected deity is eternal and supplies no exclusion claim about all other beings to which the reservation would apply. I q.14 a.4 co.: The identity of divine understanding, essence and esse is stronger and more specific than the existing possession-of-intellect and proper-operation premises. Their parameters contain no equality of that act with esse. I q.2 a.3 co., quinta via: et hoc dicimus Deum: The Fifth Way's concluding name is attached to the intelligent director. Existing naming premises use an expressly fuller nominal profile. Calling the director God supplies no link to that typed naming test without showing the further properties of this witness. I q.2 a.3 co., secunda via: quam omnes Deum nominant: The conclusion names the first efficient cause. The selected case does not use first efficient cause alone as a naming criterion. The report that it is so named does not identify that cause with an already qualified case witness. I q.85 a.1 ad 2 [32018]: quantitates, ut numeri et dimensiones et figurae ... possunt considerari absque qualitatibus sensibilibus ... Plato ... omnia quae diximus abstrahi per intellectum, posuit abstracta esse secundum rem: Abstraction from sensible qualities while retaining a quantitative subject provides an epistemic distinction. The case's concrete–abstract partition uses independently specified esse in re, and the passage provides no rule placing the target values in that partition. I-II q.94 a.2 co.: Secundum se quidem quaelibet propositio dicitur per se nota, cuius praedicatum est de ratione subiecti; contingit tamen quod ignoranti definitionem subiecti, talis propositio non erit per se nota: Aquinas's distinction concerns self-evidence through knowledge of a subject account. No active floor item is the blanket claim that every predicate in a subject account is evident to its reasoners.
